chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Bukayr ibn A'yan who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who caught a gazelle and brought it into the Sanctuary (Haram), so the gazelle died in the Sanctuary. He said: 'If when he brought it in he let it go free, there is no penalty upon him; and if he kept it until it died, then upon him is the ransom (Fida).'.
If the game was not with him and was in his house, that was permissible for him and there was no harm in it. Narrated.

key_terms.الْحَرَمُ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca/Medina where hunting is restricted)
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: Ransom or compensation paid for a religious violation
key_terms.خَلَّى سَبِيلَهُ: Let it go free / released it

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for bringing a hunted animal into the Haram sanctuary?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the liability for bringing game into the Haram depends on the pilgrim's intent and action at the moment of entry: releasing it exempts one from penalty, while retaining it incurs the ransom (Fida). This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the state of the hunted animal relative to the pilgrim's control during the transition into the sacred boundary. The ruling also extends to animals already in one's home, affirming that mere possession within the residence does not constitute a violation requiring expiation.
